chunks: Tafsir al-Qummi: My father narrated to me from Hammad from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he
recited: 'Guide us to the Straight Path, the path of those You have blessed, not of those who have incurred Your wrath, nor of those who are astray.'
He said: The Maghdub Alayhim (those who have incurred wrath) are the Nussab (haters of the Ahl al-Bayt), and the Dhalin (those astray) are the Jews and Christians.

key_terms.النُّصَب: The Nussab (haters of the Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ: Those who have incurred divine wrath

ai.seo_question: Who are the 'those who have incurred wrath' and 'those astray' in Surah Al-Fatiha according to Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: This narration from Tafsir al-Qummi highlights the Qira’ah (recitation) of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), who inserted the definite article 'al-' into the phrase, reading 'the path of those You have favored' to emphasize specific groups. In this Shia interpretation, 'those who incurred wrath' refers to the Nussab (specifically the Umayyads or haters of the Ahl al-Bayt), while 'those astray' denotes the Jews and Christians, distinguishing them from the Ahl al-Bayt as the true guided path.

en.ammaar-muslim: [3/-] Tafsir al-Qummi: My father from Hammad from Hariz from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام that he (i.e.

the Imam) recited: “Ihdina l-Sirata l-Mustaqim Sirata Man An’amta Alayhim Ghayri l-Maghdhub Alayhim wa Ghayr al-Dhalin”. He (the Imam) said: The Maghdhub Alayhim (those angered upon) are the Nussab (i.e. haters of the Ahl al-Bayt) while the Dhalin (those astray) are the Jews and Christians
